title: Why isn't Firefox distributed as a Flatpak?
post_body:
Since the philosophy behind Fedora Atomic is to keep only the essentials in the base system using rpm-ostree, why is Firefox installed by default instead of being provided as a Flatpak?

I don't like the Fedora-packaged version of Firefox, mainly because the fedora.org start page bug causes my custom settings to be reset after some updates.

What is the difference between removing the package with rpm-ostree uninstall and using rpm-ostree override? 

Which approach is recommended if I want to remove the rpm-ostree version completely, as if it had never been installed?
evidence_or_note: The main request concerns Firefox packaging and how to remove its Fedora package; the settings bug is background.

title: FF 145 title bar not displayed (Windows)
post_body:
Firefox 145 (release version, not beta/developer) is available. Upon upgrading, I noticed that the title bar (at least in Windows) is gone. It's also annoying not to have window controls (minimize, resize/restore, close) available.

People who don't display the title bar by default won't (I think) see a problem. For people who (like me) do, there is a fix (or two).

 1. You can customize the toolbar (right-click in the tab bar or menu bar (if you have it enabled) to turn off the title bar. The window controls will appear in the tab bar (or menu bar, if that's enabled). Re-enabling the title bar restores the title bar, but only for the current session.
 2. Turn off the title bar and leave it off (at least until the bug is patched).

HTH
evidence_or_note: On Windows, Firefox 145 loses the title bar. Turning the title-bar setting off or back on is an offered workaround with an observed outcome.

title: fedora failing to boot after unlocking disk
post_body:
I dualbooted fedora kde and windows 11 onto my computer, i have been using both of them fine with almost no issues for about a two or three months now. recently i saw that there was a new update for gnome and many other applications, i installed the update and it told me in order to finish the update it needed the computer to restart. I restarted my computer, unlocked the disk encryption, waited for around 4-5 minutes on the fedora loading screen. after this it said „warning: /dev/disk/by-uuid/etc does not exist”. I have tried to run an older version of the kernel, i tried to identify the drive with blkid (it was not identified). Windows and fedora are both dualbooted to the same drive but windows does not have an issue, so i figure it is not a physical issue with the drive, would anyone have any advice or ideas on what to do next?

update: solved the issue, there was an issue regenerating the intramfs, my camera, and an issue with the nvidia drivers not downloading correctly
evidence_or_note: Fedora boot fails after unlocking the disk and shows the quoted UUID warning. An older kernel was tried; blkid found no drive, a diagnostic result rather than a remedy outcome.
